children: U.S. stocks have nearly caught up with markets outside the U.S. in year-to-date price performance, according to
, who said in a post on X that the two had both gained 15.12%.
The chart showed the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF
up 15.13% and the Vanguard FTSE All-World ex-US ETF
up 15.21%, leaving ex-U.S. stocks marginally ahead.

The data showed that the gap was much wider earlier in the year, with VTI falling sharply in late March to roughly 7% below its starting level, while VEU declined less. The two subsequently recovered, with their year-to-date performances converging by October.
The figures shown on the chart are price-only and exclude dividends.
